scope: Frame-only review of the R8 native video edit, compared with previously inspected R7 native and final opening contact samples.

observations.observation: The sustained grin is reduced. At 4.500 the cheeks and eyes are less lifted and squeezed than in R7; the expression reads closer to attentive speech. Some light smiling remains at 4.250.

A light, broadly bilateral smile remains. The 5.250 pause sample has an open mouth with teeth visible and does not clearly show the requested tiny closed-lip, one-corner smirk. The sparse samples cannot rule out a brief smirk elsewhere in the 5.120–5.500 pause.
The cheeks and eyes are more relaxed than R7 through the sampled With AI interval, with less carried smile. The mouth remains free to take rounded and open speaking shapes.

continuity: No gross visible face, glasses, hair, clothing or room drift in the eight samples. Mouth shapes differ from R7; their synchronization is not assessed here.
assessment: Useful partial improvement for review, rather than a clear overall miss: it reduces the sustained grin and releases the smile through With AI. The specific one-corner smirk after the admission is not established and the 5.250 sample still reads as a small smile.
restoration_implication: The visual evidence supports retaining this as a review candidate. A lip-sync restoration may change the mouth shape again and should not be assumed to create the missing smirk or prove naturalness.
limits: No audio or normal-speed playback was assessed.
Sparse stills do not establish exact expression onset, duration, perceived authenticity or phoneme synchronization.
approval_status: No owner acceptance or production-gate change.
